MONTREAL 


1993 ANNUAL REPORT 


The Montreal YMCA 
The Montreal YMCA Foundation 


Message from the Chairman of the Board and the President and Chief Executive Officer 
of the Montreal YMCA, 
Messrs. Marcel Cété and Michael Goldbloom 


For Montreal, 1992-93 was a difficult year in economic terms. For the YMCA, it was a year in which 
there were myriad challenges. However, as it has in the past, the YMCA rose to the challenges and 
demonstrated true leadership. 


One of the most important issues during the year was the restructuring of the Montreal YMCA’s finances. 
Over the years, the Montreal YMCA had accumulated a significant debt with the Bank of Montreal, 
mainly within the framework of the planned redevelopment of its downtown community centre. 
Following the collapse of the Montreal real-estate market, the YMCA not only found itself unable to 
undertake this project, but it was also burdened by a debt which threatened to paralyse its operations. 


After two years of negotiations in a spirit of close cooperation with the Bank of Montreal, we finally 
concluded an agreement for the restructuring of our debt. The YMCA emerged from this experience 
stronger than before, with a financial basis that will allow it to pursue its social mission for another 142 
years. 


Now that this agreement has been signed, we are ready to pursue the planning for the redevelopment of 
our Downtown community centre. 


The YMCA is a community organization which is self-financing. We are, therefore, pleased to note that 
revenues from this past year’s operations exceeded our projections and that on a cash basis we have 
produced a surplus. This did not prevent us, however, from intensifying our community action in 
response to the difficult economic climate prevaling in Montreal. For example, the number of individuals 
and families who benefited from reduced rates, due to their difficult financial situations, increased 
significantly without unduly affecting the financial performance of the YMCA. 


For 142 years now, the Montreal YMCA has based its actions on the respect of the individual, without 
any form of discrimination, and has recognized that partnerships are the cornerstone of its activities. 
These guiding principles proved to be extremely valid for the year which has just ended. 


Furthermore, within the framework of the Year of Intercultural and Interracial Harmony declared by the 
Mayor of Montreal, Mr. Jean Doré, the YMCA adopted a policy on cultural diversity. This initiative 
symbolizes the determination of the Association to reflect the new reality of Montreal, through the 
composition of both its staff members and its team of volunteers. 


Kamp Kanawana, which enjoys a special stature within the activities of the YMCA, is celebrating its 
100th anniversary this year. The Kamp has always strived to develop a sense of responsibility among 
young people. Its longevity as a residential camp clearly demonstrates that it has evolved over the years, 
without losing sight of its educational mission with young people. 


Within the context of their social obligations, municipalities are facing the same challenges as we are in 
the present difficult economic climate. Like the YMCA, the municipalities must be innovative and need 
to collaborate with resources within the community. Consequently, it is in an extraordinary spirit of 
partnership that the City of Montreal and the YMCA have reached an agreement for the redevelopment 
of our community centre on Park Avenue. Thanks to this partnership, the citizens of this community will 
benefit next year from a new, ultra-modern community centre. 


For the City, it was a question of redesignating budgets which had already been earmarked for new 
recreational facilities in this district. For the YMCA, it was a question of maintaining a community 
presence which dates back over seventy-five years of involvement in this Montreal neighbourhood, which 
is characterised by a very high level of poverty and a large number of single-parent families. Thanks to 
volunteers from the area, the involvement of the community and the collaboration of the City of 
Montreal, the community centre on Park Avenue will resume its activities in a new building, and will 
be ready to tackle another seventy-five years of challenges. 


There is no need to list all the achievements of the Montreal YMCA over the course of this past year. 
To do so would risk overshadowing the most important factor contributing to our success from one year 
to the next, namely the day-to-day commitment of thousands of volunteers and staff in their own 
communities to improve the quality of life of Montrealers, and to help their fellow citizens who have to 
overcome difficult situations. 


If the Montreal YMCA did not exist, we would definitely have to invent it! 


Rectige Meee ha 


Marcel Cété Michael Goldbloom 
Chairman of the Board President and Chief Executive Officer 


We wish to express our gratitude to Samson Bélair/Deloitte & Touche for their on-going support, and 
our particular appreciation to the Bank of Montreal for its commitment to the Montreal YMCA. 


,

Message from the Chairman of the Board of the Montreal YMCA Foundation, 
Mr. John E. Cleghorn 


Established in 1983, the Montreal YMCA Foundation has just ended its tenth year of operation, and it 
is my great pleasure to report on its activities during fiscal 1992-93. 


Thanks to a Board of Directors composed of dynamic, committed members, the Foundation succeeded 
in maintaining profitable fund-raising activities. I wish to express a heartfelt thanks to each and everyone 
of them, as well as to the members of several related committees:

Governors 


In October 1992, the Foundation appointed Mr. Maurice A. Massé as a Governor of our Corporation. 


The Gabrielle and Maurice A. Massé Award 


On April 28, 1993, the Heritage Club held its tenth annual banquet. During the evening, Mr. William 
Ridley received the Gabrielle and Maurice A. Massé award which is bestowed to an individual or couple 
who, over the years, has made an important contribution to the Montreal YMCA. 


Recognized for his loyalty, reliability and eternal optimism, William Ridley has been part of our large 
YMCA family since 1935, when he first participated in the programs of the Westmount YMCA. After 
having worked as an active volunteer both at the Quebec and Westmount YMCAs, he was a member of 
the Metropolitan Board of Directors from 1973 to 1989. Since he was convinced a foundation was vital 
for the YMCA, he became one of the founding members of our Foundation. William Ridley has been 
a member of the Board since 1985 and is currently Co-Chairman of the Investments, Endowment and 
Planned Giving Committee. 


Through its mission, the Foundation has committed itself to ensure the future of the YMCA and ensure 
the implementation of long-term fund-raising programs, thus allowing the Montreal Association to 
continue to play its important roles within its constituency. Once again, this year, the successful 
activities of the Foundation confirm that the YMCA can count on the undying support of the Montreal 
community. 


John E. Cleghorn 


Message from the President of the Montreal YMCA Foundation, 
Mr. Claude Lemay 


It is my pleasure to inform you on the activities of the Foundation, as regards its fund-raising programs 
and special events for fiscal 1992-93. 


Investments, Endowment and Planned Giving 


Under the chairmanship of Mr. Maurice A. Massé, the committee responsible for the endowment and 
planned-giving program continued its hard work to preserve the heritage of the YMCA. Therefore, it 
is with great pleasure that the Foundation welcomed 9 new members to the Heritage Club. Supervised 
by the investments sub-committee, which is presided over by Mr. William Ridley, investments from the 
endowment fund generated a book value of $1,533,097. Interest and dividends from these investments 
totalled $108,252. This amount was transferred to the YMCA, according to the provisions of the 
designated and nondesignated funds. As regards the endowment and planned-giving funds, these have 
been evaluated at $1,200,000. 


Annual Sustaining Membership Campaign 


Under the co-chairmanship of Messrs. Claude Lemay and Robert S. Vineberg, the annual Sustaining 
Membership Campaign succeeded in raising close to $150,000. The funds obtained during this campaign 
serve mainly for repairs and replacements in the facilities of the Montreal- YMCA. Part of this money 
is also committed to international-development projects. The success of this fund-raising campaign was 
guaranteed, thanks to the philanthropic spirit of hundreds of volunteers and staff members, as well as the 
generous contributions of over 1,500 donors. 


Y-A-Thon 


The Y-A-Thon week was held from November 23 to November 29, 1992. Organized by a dynamic team 
of YMCA volunteers and staff members, with a view to raise funds for the purchase of equipment, this 
event allowed the branches of the Association to collect a total of $61,693. We wish to extend a sincere 
thanks to Nora Beverages Inc. for its participation as a major sponsor of this campaign. 


Benefit Performance 


Under the honorary chairmanship of Mr. Luc Plamondon, the Foundation held its annual benefit evening 
on Friday, December 4, 1992, in Théatre Maisonneuve, at Place des Arts. This year, we honoured the 
late composer Michel Berger’s work by presenting the rock opera "La Légende de Jimmy". The event, 
whose goal was to raise funds to help finance the youth programs and activities of the YMCA, allowed 
us to raise a total of $40,000. We wish to express our sincere thanks to our sponsors, namely: Hydro- 
Québec, Télé-Direct (Publications) Inc. and St. Lawrence Cement, as well as Pratt & Whitney 
Canada Inc. and the Société des alcools du Québec, for providing the buffet and wine for the cocktail 
following the performance. 


10 


Visit of Mr. Mikhail S. Gorbatchev 


During Mr. Gorbatchev’s visit to Montreal, on March 29, 1993, the Foundation was offered an 
exceptional partnership with Le Groupe Columbia, official organizer of Mr. Gorbatchev’s Montreal visit. 
In fact, at the request of the University of Calgary, he agreed to undertake a national tour, with a view 
to help raise funds for the creation of a chair on international studies to be accessible to all young 
Canadians. The profits generated by the banquet, at which Mr. Gorbatchev was the guest speaker, were 
shared by the University of Calgary and the Montreal YMCA through its Foundation. In addition, the 
firm Brockhouse & Cooper took advantage of this unique opportunity to invite Mr. Gorbatchev to a 
private dinner. As a result, this extraordinary day allowed the Foundation to raise a total of $50,800, 
of which $37,000 was placed in an endowment fund. 


Bill-Lewis Spring Race 


On April 25, 1993, the Downtown branch held its 14th consecutive Bill Lewis Spring Race. Close to 
800 runners participated in this event, whose success can be attributed to a team of over 150 volunteers. 
For the first time this year, the receipts from the race, that is $5,000, served to subsidize children from 
disadvantaged families who, otherwise, would not have been able to attend camp here, at Kamp 
Kanawana, or in Quito, in Ecuador. Thank you to Pharmaprix and Boutique Courir de Longueuil, 
for their sponsorships. 


Golf Tournament 


On May 31, 1993, the organizing committee of the YMCA golf tournament, which was presided over 
by Mr. Réal Carritre, held its eight tournament, under the honorary chairmanship of Mrs. Jocelyne 
Bourassa. Through this event, which brought 160 golfers together at the Pinegrove Golf Club, in 
Saint-Luc, we succeeded in raising $42,000 which was committed to the youth programs of the Montreal 
YMCA. We extend a heartfelt thanks to the patrons of honour of this tournament for their generous 
contributions: the Royal Bank of Canada, Bell Québec, St. Lawrence Cement, du Maurier Ltd., the 
Fédération des caisses populaires Desjardins de Montréal et de l’Ouest-du-Québec, Merck Frosst 
Canada Inc., Provigo Distribution Inc., Sony Canada Ltd., and Ultramar Canada Inc. We also 
wish to thank the 29 sponsors and the various corporations which generously offered door prizes. 


Finally, I wish to thank all the employees, volunteers and friends of the Montreal YMCA who, once 
again, through their collective efforts have helped guarantee the future of our Montreal Association. 


—F 


Claude Lemay
